entries.title: Psalms 144:1
entries.author: R. A. Torrey (editor)
entries.content:
1 David blesses God for his mercy both to him and to man. 5 He prays that God would powerfully deliver him from his enemies. 9 He promises to praise God. 11 He prays for the happy state of the kingdom.

(Title.) A Psalm of David.Calmet and others think that this Psalm was composed by David after the death of Absalom; and from a collation of it with Ps 18, in which the same ideas and form of expression occur, there can be no doubt of both having proceeded from the same pen, and that David was the author.

my strength. Heb. my rock. 18:2,31; 71:3; 95:1; De 32:30,31; Isa 26:4; *marg: Isa 45:24 teacheth. 18:34; 44:3,4; 60:12; 2Sa 22:35; 2Co 10:4; Eph 6:10,11 to war. or, to the war, etc.

entries.title: Psalms 144:2
entries.author: R. A. Torrey (editor)
entries.content: My goodness. or, mercy. my fortress. 2Sa 22:2,3,40-48; Jer 16:19 who subdueth. 18:47; 110:3

entries.title: Psalms 144:3

entries.title: Psalms 144:12

entries.content: as plants. 115:14,15; 127:4,5; 128:3; Isa 44:3-5; La 4:2 as corner stones. Job 42:15; Pr 31:10-27; Isa 3:16-24 polished. Heb. cut. the similitude. So 8:8,9; 1Pe 3:3-6

entries.title: Psalms 144:13
entries.author: R. A. Torrey (editor)
entries.content: our garners. 107:37,38; Le 26:5,10; De 28:8; Mal 3:10; Lu 12:16-20 all manner of store. Heb. from kind to kind. our sheep. Ge 30:29-31; De 7:13,14; 8:3; 28:4

entries.title: Psalms 144:14
entries.author: R. A. Torrey (editor)
entries.content: strong to labour. Heb. able to bear burdens, or loaden withflesh. no breaking in. De 28:7,25; Jud 5:8; 6:3,6; 1Sa 13:17-23; 31:7; Jer 13:17-19; 14:18 La 1:4-6; Zec 8:3-5
